posts.author: Tom B.
posts.content_md: Looks like a great deal. US only shipping, though. Focal length (29"") is very short compared to the usual telescope mirrors - about f/2 versus f/5-10 for telescopes. I wonder if this would cause unacceptable problems with distortion when used off-axis, as it inevitably would be used in holography. But it would sure make a nice compact layout.

posts.author: dave battin
posts.content_md: typically all spherical/parabolic mirrors will give distortions when used off axis (unless ground and polished for off axis use $). my 10 inch 5.6 F parabolic shows distortions when i project my image to far .... as far as display holography is concerned this is acceptable (in my opinion of course)!LOL

posts.content_md: its nice to know the system works! Tom M from the forum won this little beauty.......

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md:
Wow, That went cheap. Just for the record there is no problems using spherical mirrors off axis. Parabolic mirrors have better correction on axis but at some critical angle they perform worse off axis. If you get a book on optics (Like the one by Hecht) it will give you the equations to evaluate a mirrors performance.

[http://search.barnesandnoble.com/bookse ... XT=Y&itm=5](http://search.barnesandnoble.com/booksearch/isbnInquiry.asp?userid=0g3fpBrAwm&isbn=0805385665&TXT=Y&itm=5)
